claim: The exec drivers stop at a reached, un-closed horizon REGARDLESS of the once-flag's state. P3 only probes a fresh project (the tick WAKES replan_pending). When a previous tick already wrote .hb/.replan-alerted, the tick now SLEEPS {reason: replan_waiting} — and both hb-exec.js run and hb exec run must still terminate with a nonzero exit whose stop line names the horizon (replan_pending / replan_waiting), never 'HB-EXEC DONE' and never an exit-0 'HB-EXEC IDLE' that reads to a caller as a finished or idle project. In both the fresh and the pre-alerted run the backend command is never invoked (HB_EXEC_BACKEND=script HB_EXEC_CMD='touch INVOKED' leaves no INVOKED file) and no event is appended to events.jsonl.
violation: On a reached-horizon fixture, run one tick (any runtime) so .replan-alerted exists, then run each exec driver: an exit status of 0, a line 'HB-EXEC DONE' or 'HB-EXEC IDLE: replan_waiting' with exit 0, an INVOKED file created by the backend, or a grown events.jsonl on either runtime falsifies this constraint; so does tests/horizon.sh m4 passing while this pre-alerted shape is unprobed.

claim: The replan wake has exactly one side effect and it is runtime-portable. On a reached, un-closed horizon, across at least three ticks in ANY interleaving of tick.sh and tick.py (including with STUCK_TICKS=1): events.jsonl is byte-identical to its pre-tick bytes; the only new entry under .hb is .replan-alerted, whose content is exactly the horizon phase id with no trailing newline and identical whichever runtime wrote it; exactly ONE wake occurs in total — a flag written by tick.sh is honored by tick.py as already-alerted (it sleeps replan_waiting) and vice versa; no .noprogress-alerted, .stuck-alerted or .deadlock-alerted appears (a pre-existing .deadlock-alerted is removed by the replan branch on both); HB_NOTIFY_CMD (tick.sh) fires exactly once with $1=replan_pending and $3=<phase id>; the wake's data.phase equals the resolver's phase and each sleep is {reason: replan_waiting, phase: <id>} on both. The flag is runtime litter: a bootstrap that initialises git itself lists .hb/.replan-alerted in the project .gitignore (git check-ignore .hb/.replan-alerted exits 0).
violation: A changed events.jsonl hash after the ticks, a flag whose bytes differ between runtimes or carry a newline, a second wake when the runtimes alternate (sh then py, or py then sh), a stray .noprogress-alerted/.stuck-alerted, a notifier that fires twice or with the wrong $1/$3, a sleep payload missing phase on either runtime, or git check-ignore failing for .hb/.replan-alerted after a git-mode bootstrap.

claim: The horizon_closed projection and the resolver read hostile input identically and never throw. A horizon_closed event whose phase is missing, null, a number or the empty string is ignored by BOTH projections (state.json keeps NO horizon_closed key, the resolver still returns replan_pending); duplicate closes of one phase collapse to a single entry at its FIRST occurrence position; a close for a phase id that is not in the dag is still projected (both agree, byte-equal after the proj_compare normalisation, e.g. ['ZZ','H2'] for the sequence ZZ, H2, ZZ); and a hand-edited state.json whose horizon_closed is a string, object, number or null makes neither resolver throw — both read it as 'no closes' and return replan_pending with identical keys.
violation: Either projection grows a horizon_closed key (or crashes) from a malformed event, the two runtimes order or dedupe the list differently, either projection drops the unknown-phase close while the other keeps it, or a non-list state.horizon_closed produces a TypeError/Traceback or an all_done verdict on either resolver.

claim: The lint type rule is exact where JS and Python truthiness disagree: a horizon value of 1, 0, 1.0, "true", "yes", null, [] or {} is an ERROR on BOTH lints with byte-identical message text '[<pid>] horizon must be true or false (the knowledge-horizon marker)' and exit 1/1; EXACTLY one such error per offending phase (two offending phases yield two lines, each naming its own id, in plan order); a phase with a missing or non-string id renders the prefix '[?]' on both; and hb-audit.js / audit.py neither crash nor emit any horizon-related finding on a dag whose marker is non-boolean (the type rule is lint's alone).
violation: Any listed value passes one lint and fails the other (the isinstance(bool) vs typeof split, or 0/[]/{} read as absent), a differing message byte, an error count that is not one-per-offending-phase, a prefix other than '[?]' for a degenerate id, or an audit crash / horizon finding on the non-boolean dag.

claim: speculative_tail's edge semantics are mirrored exactly, in both the text line and the --json finding (phase anchor, tail[], cut): (a) marker-independence — a plan carrying "horizon": true on its last phase AND >= 2 unverified trailing live phases STILL fires (the cure is cutting the tail, not flagging it); (b) a gate_exit naming a gate absent from dag.gates counts unverified; (c) a gate whose criteria is a string, object or null, or whose criterion cmd is a non-string, counts unverified without a crash; (d) a PARKED phase lying between the verified head and the tail is skipped — the cut is the last verified LIVE phase and the tail is contiguous over live phases; (e) unverified middle phases followed by a verified LAST phase stay quiet (trailing only); (f) a plan whose only verified phase is parked stays quiet (no live gated head); (g) a four-phase tail yields exactly ONE finding naming all four ids in plan order, anchored on the first tail id, with identical tail[] and cut on both runtimes.
violation: Any shape (a)-(g) fires on one runtime and not the other, fires more than once, names a different cut or tail order, anchors on a different phase, crashes on the hostile criteria shapes, or the JSON extras (tail, cut) differ between node and python.

claim: The report's horizon line follows the LAST LIVE phase and the close's phase scope, byte-identically on both runtimes, exit 0 in every state: after a recorded close of H2 and an append of a flagged H3, the line reads 'Horizon: H3 (planned) …' (not H2's closed-by), then 'Horizon: H3 REACHED …' naming both moves once H3 completes, then 'Horizon: H3 closed by <actor>: <reason>' taken from the LAST horizon_closed event FOR H3; parking H3 makes the line fall back to H2's closed-by line; an appended UNFLAGGED last phase prints no horizon line at all (the stale H2 flag is inert); parking the flagged phase itself prints no line. The closed-by line reproduces the recorded reason verbatim — quotes, ampersands, angle brackets and non-ASCII dashes included — and when HB_ACTOR is unset the actor is 'unknown' in the event, the close's stdout and the report on both runtimes.
violation: A report line naming the wrong phase or state for any step of the H2-closed-then-H3 sequence, a horizon line on the unflagged-append or parked-flag shapes, a reason or actor altered or truncated between event and report, a differing line byte between runtimes, or a nonzero report exit.

claim: The close verb's perimeter spans every LIVE gate and its CLI edge shapes are fail-closed on both runtimes: an open regate (declared, unanswered-in-log, or rearmed without a fresh criteria-pinned pass) on an EARLIER live phase's gate — not the horizon phase's own — refuses the close naming that gate, with no event; a whitespace-only --reason is refused with no event; 'hb horizon' with no subaction and 'hb horizon open' exit nonzero with no event; an accepted close appends EXACTLY one line, a horizon_closed event carrying event/phase/reason/ts/actor, whose reason is the quoted --reason value verbatim (whitespace-trimmed); hb doctor and hb diagnose stay exit-0 and problem-free on a reached open horizon and after a valid close; and under the drift tripwire (a completed live gate's criteria edited after its pin, doctor red) the close behaves IDENTICALLY on both runtimes — same accept/refuse outcome, same exit class, same events.jsonl delta — whichever way the design falls.
violation: A close accepted while GATE_H1 (the earlier gate) has a declared, unanswered or stale-rearmed regate; a whitespace-only reason, a missing subaction or an unknown subaction that exits 0 or appends an event; an accepted close that appends more or fewer than one line or alters the reason; a doctor/diagnose problem on the reached or closed horizon; or node and python disagreeing (accept vs refuse, or differing event counts) on the close under drift.

claim: Criteria drift outranks the horizon wake on both ticks: at a reached, un-closed horizon whose completed live gate's criteria were edited after their pinned pass, every tick (tick.sh and tick.py) wakes criteria_drift — never replan_pending — and writes no .replan-alerted; the exec drivers stop on criteria_drift there; once the drift is cured by a complete regate cycle on that gate (declare, rearm with an artifact, fresh criteria-pinned pass via gate.sh) the next tick wakes replan_pending exactly once on both runtimes and the second sleeps replan_waiting.
violation: Either tick wakes replan_pending (or sleeps replan_waiting) while the drift is live, a .replan-alerted file appears before the cure, a driver prints anything but a criteria_drift stop, or after the regate cycle plus fresh pass the replan wake fails to fire once (or fires twice) on either runtime.
